newsitem.title: CHINA: Bomb on bus kills at least two in China capital.
newsitem.headline: Bomb on bus kills at least two in China capital.

text.p: At least two people were killed and several were injured in a bomb attack on a bus in the Chinese capital Beijing during Friday's rush hour, Chinese sources said.
The explosion occurred in the Xidan shopping district in western Beijing, the sources said.
The motive for the blast was not immediately known and it was unclear whether police had made any arrests.
Uniformed and plainclothes police were seen patrolling near the Xidan Market in the area where the blast occurred.
Police set up check points around the capital, stopping and searching vehicles and checking drivers' papers.

Two weeks ago, in the restive Moslem region of Xinjiang, three bombs planted on buses blew up within minutes of each other on February 25 in an apparently coordinated attack that coincided with funeral rites in Beijing for paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
A fourth bomb failed to explode.
A pro-Beijing newspaper said on Friday that China had arrested seven suspects in the attacks in the Xinjiang regional capital Urumqi that killed nine people and wounded 74.
Exiled Uighur nationalists in neighbouring Kazakhstan claimed responsibility for the Xinjiang bombings and for a similar, previously unreported attack near the Kazakh border on Monday.
Moslem separatists want to set up an independent "East Turkestan" in Xinjiang, home to many Turkic-speaking people, including the Uighur ethnic minority.
